_comment: The canonical Oath standard library: a REVIEWED COLLECTION OF PINNED
PUBLICATION IDENTITIES. Membership means 'reviewed and selected for canonical
consumption'. It does NOT mean the Oath project owns the copyright or has
relicensed anything.
TWO MEMBERSHIP MODES, because they make different claims:
referenced          the library DEPENDS ON an existing publication. Oath makes
NO new licence assertion; evaluation consumes that
publication's own signed terms. This is the DEFAULT for
third-party work.
project-publication the project publishes the artifact under oath/* and makes
ITS OWN licence assertion. Requires separate STANDING
evidence that the project may make that grant.
WHY THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING. Terms attach to a PUBLICATION, not to an
artifact (SPEC §12.3). So republishing someone else's artifact under oath/* with
our licence is a FRESH ASSERTION BY US, not an inheritance — and the registry
notarises assertions without auditing them, so a false one would be recorded
with full cryptographic ceremony and evaluated as fact.
STANDING IS NOT NAME OWNERSHIP. Cryptographic ownership of a registry name
proves authority over the NAME. It does not establish copyright or the right to
relicense: Apache-2.0 permits redistribution subject to notice obligations and
does not make a downstream publisher the rights holder. project-publication
therefore requires evidence beyond ownership.
EACH ENTRY PINS ONE SOURCE PUBLICATION, identified by the sha256 of its exact
canonical signed octets. Deliberately NOT a survey of every publication of the
artifact: one bogus UNSTATED publication must not poison a legitimate grant, and
one bogus permissive publication must not authorise adoption. Other publications
of the same artifact remain visible provenance, never automatic inputs.
JSON rather than YAML: the Go kernel is zero-dependency by default and a
manifest it may one day read must not need a parser it cannot have.
authority_note: The project key that must hold oath/* and sign every publication under it. PUBLIC HALF ONLY — the private key is never in this repository. TEMPORARY LIMITATION: this version has no delegation, so this same key must both hold the namespace and perform CI publication. A compromised release secret would therefore control the namespace itself, not merely the right to publish into it. The intended end state is an offline authority key delegating publication to a revocable release key; until delegation exists this is recorded rather than hidden.
